findings.title: topLevelStatements() and executableSql() share a hiding place: a '--' inside a single-quoted string blinds both, hiding a widened REVOKE that no arm of the suite can detect
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Both helpers strip --[^\n]* before any string masking, and PostgreSQL does not treat -- inside a string literal as a comment. Proven in-tree under vitest with the live container: the migration widened to REVOKE ALL ON job_outbox FROM service_role reports 6 passed 0 failed, and on a throwaway clone service_role loses all seven privileges. The suite header lines 61-70 state it asserts nothing about service_role and names this text guard as the sole guard for it, so this survivor is invisible to Arms A, B and C in every environment. The code comment at lines 195-199 asserts the two checks 'cannot share a hiding place' and the helper doc-comment at lines 104-106 asserts this exact hazard 'would fail loudly rather than silently'; both are false. Not an equivalent mutant and not an unexecuted branch.

findings.title: block comments are PostgreSQL token separators and no helper strips them, so DISABLE/**/ROW LEVEL SECURITY, CREATE/**/POLICY and FORCE/**/ROW LEVEL SECURITY all evade the three phrase guards
findings.arbiter_reasoning: normalizedSql() collapses \s+ but a block comment is not whitespace. All three mutants apply cleanly on PostgreSQL 16.14 and change the catalogue (relrowsecurity false, one policy, relforcerowsecurity true respectively) while every text guard returns zero failures; the plain spellings are all caught, so the mutants are semantically meaningful and the branch is executed. This is pass 3's whitespace-literal defect one level up. The catalogue arms catch all three on a re-provisioned container, but the DB lane skips silently without TEST_DATABASE_POOL_URL — observed this pass as 3 passed, 3 skipped, exit 0 — which is the configuration this guard exists to cover.

findings.title: normalizedSql() retains comments, so the suite's only positive assertion is satisfiable by a line comment while migration 119 stops enabling RLS
findings.arbiter_reasoning: The positive assertion toMatch(/ALTER TABLE job_outbox ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;/) reads normalizedSql(), which keeps comments. Replacing the ALTER inside the guarded DO block with 'PERFORM 1; -- ALTER TABLE job_outbox ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;' applies cleanly, leaves relrowsecurity false on a clone that began with the client grants live, and returns zero failures across all four text guards. Not equivalent — the mutant removes the migration's whole effect. Executed on every invocation. The helper split the file documents as load-bearing is what creates the hole: the one guard that must prove a statement exists reads the text where comments still live.

findings.title: false coverage claim: the '>= 7' assertion is on the TABLE privilege list and cannot detect a fifth COLUMN privilege, so Arm C's stated fail-loud protection does not exist
findings.reason: The only count assertion in the file counts acldefault('r', owner), measured at 7 on the PG16.14 container and 8 on the PG17.6 Supabase projects. A PostgreSQL adding a fifth column privilege would take that to 9 and >= 7 would still pass; columnPrivileges carries no assertion at all. The four-element set is nonetheless correct today on both versions, and the >= 7 assertion does soundly protect Arm B from its empty-CROSS-JOIN fail-open. Behavioural replacement: assert columnPrivileges.length === 4, or probe has_column_privilege for newly-accepted names.

findings.title: the one privilege-shape cell no arm covers: membership granted WITH INHERIT FALSE, SET TRUE (PG16+), reachable via SET ROLE
findings.reason: Measured across 13 grant shapes on a throwaway clone: every {table, column} x {direct, PUBLIC, inherited, nested-inherited, predefined role, WITH GRANT OPTION} cell is caught by at least one arm. Non-inherited membership returns A=0 B=0 C=0 for both table and column grants, because has_table_privilege and has_column_privilege use USAGE (inherit) semantics. Recorded rather than raised: it requires an unusual future GRANT form plus a SET ROLE vector through PostgREST.
